question: In patients with rotator cuff tears, is cellular therapy (e.g. mesenchymal stem cells, bone marrow aspirate, platelet-rich plasma) beneficial compared with controls for healing and clinical outcomes?
source: SYNERGY dataset Muthu_2022; 'Is cellular therapy beneficial in management of rotator cuff tears?' (World J Meta-Anal 2022, doi:10.13105/wjma.v10.i3.162); gold = label_included==1 rows with DOI via [AID]
notes: Created with make_fixture.py. No baseline strategy: use evals/generate.py (Phase 2). Harness reports reachable vs. unreachable gold separately.

version_change.decision_source: Evaluation fixture author; scope derived from the source systematic review.

review.question: In patients with rotator cuff tears, is cellular therapy (e.g. mesenchymal stem cells, bone marrow aspirate, platelet-rich plasma) beneficial compared with controls for healing and clinical outcomes?

framework.name: PICO
framework.rationale: A clinical effectiveness question; PICO separates the population (rotator cuff tears) and intervention (cellular therapy), which drive retrieval, from comparator and outcomes, which are screening-only to protect recall.

slots.label: Population
slots.description: Patients with rotator cuff tears undergoing repair.

slots.label: Intervention
slots.description: Cellular therapy: mesenchymal stem cells, bone marrow aspirate concentrate, platelet-rich plasma, adipose- or tendon-derived cells.

slots.label: Comparator
slots.description: Standard repair or control without cellular augmentation.

slots.label: Outcome
slots.description: Structural healing, retear, pain, and functional scores.

inclusion.label: Rotator cuff tear
inclusion.description: Patients with a rotator cuff tear (partial- or full-thickness) or undergoing rotator cuff repair.

inclusion.label: Cellular therapy
inclusion.description: The intervention delivers a cellular therapy (MSCs, bone marrow aspirate concentrate, PRP, adipose- or tendon-derived cells) as biologic augmentation.

inclusion.label: Control comparison
inclusion.description: Comparison against a control or standard repair without cellular augmentation.

inclusion.label: Clinical or structural outcome
inclusion.description: Reports a healing/retear, pain, or functional outcome.

inclusion.label: Comparative clinical study
inclusion.description: A randomized or otherwise comparative clinical study in humans.

exclusion.label: Not rotator cuff
exclusion.description: Not a rotator cuff tear/repair population (e.g. other tendon or joint).

exclusion.label: Not cellular therapy
exclusion.description: The intervention is not a cellular therapy.

exclusion.label: No control comparison
exclusion.description: No comparison group without cellular augmentation.

concepts.label: Rotator cuff tear/repair
concepts.definition: The population and anatomical target: rotator cuff tears and their surgical repair, including the supraspinatus tendon.
concepts.rationale: A stable essential concept anchoring every eligible study to the rotator cuff.

concepts.label: Cellular therapy / biologic augmentation
concepts.definition: The intervention: cell-based biologic augmentation, spanning mesenchymal stem cells, bone marrow aspirate concentrate, platelet-rich plasma, and adipose- or tendon-derived cells.
concepts.rationale: A stable essential concept with varied vocabulary (stem cells, MSC, BMAC, PRP), so it needs broad synonym expansion.

properties.label: Control / standard repair comparator
properties.instructions: Confirm at screening that the study has a control or standard-repair comparison. Do not add a comparator AND block.
properties.recall_rationale: Comparator wording is inconsistent and often absent from abstracts; a comparator block would drop eligible trials.

properties.label: Healing / clinical outcome
properties.instructions: Confirm at screening that a structural-healing, retear, pain, or functional outcome is reported. Do not add an outcome AND block.
properties.recall_rationale: Outcome vocabulary is varied and frequently not in the abstract; an outcome block is a recall bottleneck.

properties.label: Comparative clinical design
properties.instructions: Confirm at screening that the study is a comparative clinical study. Apply no methodological search filter.
properties.recall_rationale: Design filters miss poorly indexed surgical trials; screen for design instead of filtering the search.

decisions.label: Methodological (study-design) filter
decisions.rationale: Recall-first evaluation build; study design is confirmed at screening, not by a search-time hedge.

decisions.label: Database limits
decisions.rationale: No language, age, species, publication-status, or date limits for the recall-first evaluation build.

date_boundaries.rationale: No date boundaries; the evaluation scores against a fixed gold set.

recall.policy: Recall first; decline the optional no-seed heuristic during evaluation because hidden gold is scored independently.

workload.policy: Do not narrow solely because retrieval is large.
workload.selection_rule: Workload may choose only among variants that meet the held-out recall requirement.

protocol_status: tightened; lock-validated and compiled. Naive 2-block scope (rotator cuff x cellular therapy) recalls 6/6 gold at ~1.2k hits.
